Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Moderate thermals with peak w* up to 559 ft/min and ceilings reaching 10,676 ft AGL at Rainbow Ridge. Sharp lapse rates (~10 °C/km) demand advanced pilot skills. Widespread mid-high cloud (70–90%) suppresses peak heating but no overdevelopment. Variable winds shift from SW to NW through the day, making site selection and timing critical; afternoon/evening ridge soaring possible at Duck Hill and Hallelujah.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury Grade: Marginal — preferred SE wind only briefly 12–1pm, otherwise cross from the south then increasing NW flow; peak w* 421 fpm, thermal ceiling 6,091 ft AGL. Best window 11am–1pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — wind within preferred SW–W arc from 10am into evening; peak w* 492 fpm, ceiling 9,962 ft AGL. High cloud 84% but thermals still organize. Soaring window 11am–4pm, evening ridge flying possible until 8pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — SW wind all day well outside the S–SE launch tolerance; only a late-afternoon shift when thermals have died. Peak w* 405 fpm, ceiling 5,892 ft. Cloud 88%. Not recommended.
  • McClellan: Favorable — wind direction stays within SW–S preferred range through 1pm, providing a solid late-morning window. Peak w* 515 fpm, ceiling 6,583 ft AGL. Best window 10am–1pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • West McClellan: Favorable — afternoon winds settle into good W–NW direction; thermals peak 1–5pm. Peak w* 435 fpm, ceiling 5,447 ft AGL. Best window 1pm–5pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — wind inside the S–SE preferred sector only until mid-morning, then turns SW and out of tolerance; strong thermals arrive too late. Peak w* 462 fpm, ceiling 8,288 ft. Brief window 9am–11am. Hazardous layer shear 7 mph near 8,500 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal — ridge lift works with NE–ENE wind only through late morning; best thermals (peak 559 fpm, ceiling 10,676 ft) occur in afternoon with cross NW flow. Thermal-only flight possible but bulk shear 18 mph and low-level speed shear 5 mph elevate risk. Ridge window 9am–12pm, cautious thermal window 2–5pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — NW–N wind direction aligns from 2pm onward, overlapping with solid afternoon thermals and continuing usable ridge lift into the evening. Peak w* 487 fpm, ceiling 7,694 ft AGL. Flying window 2pm–9pm. Sharp lapse rate – advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — no thermals (w* 0, ceiling <760 ft AGL) and wind direction never within the preferred SW range. Not flyable.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals — lapse rate 9.7–10.1 °C/km across all sites; suitable for advanced/expert pilots only.
  • Low-level wind shear — hazardous layer speed shear ≥5 mph present at Hallelujah (at 9,668 ft AGL), Peavine (8,464 ft AGL), Rainbow Ridge (1,192 ft AGL), and Duck Hill (6,773 ft AGL). Bulk shear reaches 18 mph at Rainbow Ridge.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence — moderate SW–W flow in the afternoon will create lee-side turbulence downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range ridgelines; exercise caution in those zones.
  • High cloud cover — 70–90% sky coverage may slow surface heating and delay or weaken thermal development; adjust timing expectations accordingly.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
